speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your bleeding issues, could you tell me how old you are and if you have had any recent fevers, bone pain, or unexplained bruising? Also, is there a family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Does the child have any history of recent viral illnesses, and have you noticed any swelling in the abdomen or lymph nodes? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Platelet_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the normal platelet count, I need to check how well the blood is clotting. REQUEST TEST: Prothrombin_Time_and_Partial_Thromboplastin_Time

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the platelet count and clotting times are normal, this points toward a defect in platelet function or a vascular issue rather than a clotting factor deficiency. I will order a specific test to evaluate how well the platelets are working together.

REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time_and_Platelet_Function_Analyzer

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding time: Prolonged. Platelet Function Analyzer: Abnormal aggregation with ADP, epinephrine, and collagen. ELISA Binding Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GPIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results showing a deficiency in GPIIb/IIIa receptors are diagnostic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
